name: Pablo Jarillo-Herrero
description: Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's group at MIT created the field of twistronics with the 2018 discovery that two graphene sheets twisted to approximately 1.1 degrees — the 'magic angle' — become a correlated-electron superconductor, an experimental result published in Nature that generated thousands of follow-on papers and reshaped condensed matter physics. The twisted bilayer graphene platform he developed also exhibits Mott insulator and quantum anomalous Hall states tunable by gate voltage, making it a versatile analog quantum simulator. Jarillo-Herrero is a principal investigator in the DOE Energy Frontier Research Center on Quantum Matter and was awarded the 2020 Oliver Buckley Prize by the American Physical Society. He is a co-founder of HyperLight Corporation, commercializing lithium niobate photonic chips emerging from related electro-optic platform research. He received his PhD in Delft and his early career fellowships included a prestigious Miller Research Fellowship at Berkeley.
